label: Income and income structure of household-dwelling units by Information, Year and Decile
note:
Data in euros are given in the value of the latest statistical year.
Statistical unit: household-dwelling unit. 
Income concept: Disposable monetary income (incl. sales profits), per consumption unit and household-dwelling unit, main income items per household-dwelling unit. 
Consumption unit scale : Eurostat's equivalence scale (1.0 - 0.5 - 0.3).
Due to revisions to income concepts the figures for 1995 to 2009 and 2010 onwards are not fully comparable with each other.

tjt-henkiloita: Dwelling population, persons. The dwelling population comprises those persons who resided permanently in dwellings on 31 December.
modoecd_mean: The Eurostat scale (the OECD's modified scale), where the first adult in the household is assigned a weight of 1, other individuals over 13 years old are assigned a weight of 0.5, and children are assigned a weight of 0.3 (ages 0-13)
tjt-ostu:
Dividend income covers dividends from publicly and non-publicly traded companies, dividend income from partnerships, dividend income from abroad, surpluses from cooperatives, and profit shares from investment funds.
Dividend income includes a tax-free portion of the dividend income.
tjt-myvo:
Sales profits = realized capital gains - losses (negative values have been set to zerot).
Includes taxable capital gains and tax-free capital gain, when the sales prices were under 1000 euros.
saatusi: Current transfers received (sub-times according to ESSPROS-classication).
tjt-saira: Sairausajan toimeentuloturva sisältää mm. sairaus-, tartunta- ja tapaturmapäivärahat.
tjt-vamtyoky: Toimintarajoitteisuuteen liittyvät tuet sisältävät mm. työkyvyttömyyseläkkeet, kuntoutusrahan, vammaistuen sekä sotilasvammakorvaukset.
tjt-vanel: Includes national pensions, occupational pensions, and guaranteed pensions as old-age pensions
tjt-perav: Benefits for families with children include child allowances, parental allowances, home care support, and from 2010 onwards, maintenance support.
tjt-tyoel: Includes basic unemployment allowance, labour market subsidy, earnings-related unemployment benefits, pension support, start-up money, training support, adult education support, and alternating compensation.
tjt-asutu: General housing allowance, housing allowance for pensioners and student housing supplement.
tjt-optuki: Study benefits include taxable study grants, vocational qualification scholarships, as well as grants and study allowances. Conscript allowances are also included in study benefits. Withdrawn student loans are not included in study benefits
tjt-muutuki: Other income  security includes income support, military assistance, interest subsidy for student loans, taxable strike assistance, register-based imputed received maintenance support and from 2024 onwards reception allowance.
tjt-ekvikturaha_mean: Equivalent income, which is the disposable monetary income of a household (or household) divided by consumption units (Eurostat scale).
tjt-ekvikturaha_med: Equivalent income, which is the disposable monetary income of a dwelling unit (or economic household) divided by consumption units (Eurostat scale). When the statistical unit is a person, equivalent income describes the level of a person's economic well-being more broadly than personal income.
korotyht: Household total interest expenses. The content for loans other than housing loans changed in 2012; see Statistics Finland's concepts and definitions for the indebtedness statistics.
